must_remember: Time is absolute in Galilean relativity, meaning $t' = t$ for all inertial observers.
The spatial position transformation along the x-axis is given by $x' = x - vt$.
Acceleration remains invariant under Galilean transformations, such that $a' = a$.
Maxwell's equations of electromagnetism are not invariant under Galilean transformations.
The velocity addition theorem in classical mechanics is expressed as $u' = u - v$.

glossary.meaning: A set of equations used to relate the space and time coordinates of two inertial frames moving at a constant relative velocity.
The assumption that the time interval between events is identical for all observers regardless of their relative motion ($t' = t$).
A reference frame in which Newton's first law of motion holds true and which moves at zero acceleration.
The classical law relating velocities measured in different inertial frames, given by $u' = u - v$.
